comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 `presenceStore: null` silently disables the live exemption instead of failing closed

`_liveIds()` maps a null store to an empty live-set (treated as "nothing is live"), while a *failing* probe aborts the sweep. The doc comment scopes null to tests, and today every production boot path wires a real store (`bin/fah_runapp.dart` for the CLI; the clean verb passes one too) — so this is hardening, not a bug.

But the PR's stated posture is fail-closed ("a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session"). A future embedder host that runs `enforceAtBoot()` without wiring a presence store would sweep live sessions while believing none are live.

Suggested: in `enforceAtBoot()`, treat `presenceStore == null` the same as a failed probe (abort with a note), or add an explicit `allowMissingPresence` flag so the test convenience is opt-in rather than the default shape.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves

   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

the unused surface.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Fixed — the boot sweep can no longer delete the session being opened

`_initializeSession()` (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart) was restructured: the resume target now resolves **before** the sweep — `_sessionNameMatches(config.sessionName)` → `_resolveSessionNameMatch` — and `_retentionBootCheck(currentSessionId: metadata?.id)` hands the resolved id to `SessionRetentionSweeper` as `currentSessionId`. The sweep still runs before the session opens (ordering unchanged), so the resume target is exempt whether it is addressed by id (unnamed sessions — the exit-hint form), by name under `keepNamed: false`, or ambiguously auto-resolved. comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Fixed — both dead surfaces are resolved (id wired, name dropped)

1. `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is now an **identity check**: in `_scanSlugDir`, a header whose `id` disagrees with the filename-derived session id is skipped with a note (`header id "…" does not match filename id "…"`) — a mismatched/foreign header can no longer make its file a sweepable unit keyed by the filename.

comments.body:

The blocker walk in `SessionRetentionSweeper.sweep` is now minimal: exempt units are sorted largest-first and added only until the held bytes reach the overflow (`remaining - cap`). `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: inside the `sessionList != null` block the clean verb no longer re-creates `io`/env/root — it reuses the enclosing `_TerminalCliIO`, `LocalExecutionEnv`, and `parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()` locals. The `FileSessionPresenceStore` wiring (including the gh-1660 `pidAlive` probe comment) is hoisted once as `sessionPresenceStore`, shared verbatim by the repair and clean branches, and `readRetention()` was hoisted to the same scope (it now also feeds the list verb's gh-1746 usage footer). The verbs cannot drift anymore.

Additionally the bin wiring is now guarded: `test/bin_main_wiring_reg_test.dart` pins `runSessionListCliCommand`, `runSessionRepairCliCommand`, and `runSessionCleanCliCommand` to the executable library — the gh-1000 take-ours-merge shape (which this branch already hit once) can no longer drop a session verb silently.
